name: @ahpd/computer
description: Disposable Docker machines for the ahpd daemon: a computer: resource provider and the tools that make, use and release one
author: Luiz Fernando Softov <lfs@softov.dev>

ahpd.title: Computer
ahpd.description: Provides isolated Docker/Container environments for agent sessions, including lifecycle management and tools.

closers: the up time of every running machine

runtime.description: Which runtime to use: docker, which makes machines, or ssh, which only lists them.

args.description: Arguments before its own, for a wrapper or a context.

ssh.description: Boxes this host reaches over ssh. Each is listed rather than made, so none can be created, started or removed here; a session on one starts its host from the ahpd this host installs in the user's own folder there.

command.description: The program that reaches a box. ssh.

args.description: Arguments before its own, for a wrapper or a jump host.

connectTimeout.description: Seconds ssh is given to reach a box before it refuses. 30 when absent.

pollSeconds.description: Seconds between checks of each box, so the up time charged for a box ends at a check rather than at the next listing. Only a listing moves the meter when absent.

machines.description: The boxes, by the name a machine id is spelled with: the entry dev02 is the machine ssh.dev02.

destination.description: What ssh is given as the host: user@host, or a name from its own config. An entry without one is not a box and is dropped.

port.description: The port, when it is not the one ssh would use.

identity.description: The private key to reach it with, when ssh would not pick one itself.

workdir.description: Where a command starts on the box. The login directory when absent, which is also where a path from this host is not.

host.description: The command that starts a nested host on the box, run as written with nothing installed. The ahpd this host installs in the user's own folder there when absent.

agents.description: The agents the box is prepared for, as a machine carries them in a label. A session of another agent is refused.

libvirt.description: How a profile with runtime libvirt makes its machines: each is a VM on its server's libvirt, a linked clone of a template disk, reached over ssh through that server.

uri.description: The libvirt connection URI for every server. qemu+ssh://<destination>/system when absent.

pool.description: The storage pool that holds the template and every VM's disk.

network.description: The libvirt network a VM is attached to.

template.description: A template's volume in the pool, which every VM's disk backs onto. When absent, a template is built from image on each server, with the parts this host's Docker builds.

image.description: The cloud image's volume in the pool, a qcow2 with cloud-init, which a template is built from. A VM is refused when neither this nor template is set.

user.description: The login a VM is made with. ahpd when absent.

disk.description: The size of a VM's disk, as virsh vol-create-as reads it. 20G when absent.

virsh.description: The virsh program and the arguments it starts with. ["virsh"] when absent.

virtInstall.description: The virt-install program and the arguments it starts with. ["virt-install"] when absent.

proxmox.description: How a profile with runtime proxmox makes its machines: each is a VM on this node, a linked clone of a template VM, reached over ssh at the address its guest agent reports, through the profile's server when it names one.

secret.description: The API token's secret. A name may be given instead of the secret, as {"$secret": "host:proxmox"}.

node.description: The node every VM is made on.

storage.description: The storage a template built here is copied onto.

bridge.description: The bridge a VM's network card is on.

template.description: The name of a template VM on the node, with cloud-init and the QEMU guest agent, which every VM is a linked clone of. When absent, a template is built from image, with the parts this host's Docker builds.

image.description: The name of a cloud-init template VM on the node, with the QEMU guest agent, which a template is built from. A VM is refused when neither this nor template is set.

user.description: The login a VM is made with. ahpd when absent.

ca.description: A PEM file on this host that the node's certificate is checked against, for a node with its own certificate authority.

env.description: Environment variables merged over the daemon's. A variable is a credential wherever the image keeps one, so each answers <set>.

image.description: The image a machine is made from when a call names none.

cpus.description: A CPU limit for every machine this host makes.

memory.description: A memory limit for every machine this host makes.

max.description: How many machines may exist at once when the agent's tool asks for one more.

prefix.description: What the name of every machine this host makes starts with.

sessionSetting.description: Whether a session setting names the machine a session runs in.

needs.description: Values for any agent's machine needs, by need name.

mounts.description: What every machine this plugin makes can see.

title.description: What the picker shows for it, a string. The profile name when absent.

description.description: One line about what it is for, a string.

image.description: The image its machines are made from, a string. The plugin's image when absent.

cpus.description: A CPU limit for its machines, a string. The plugin's cpus when absent.

memory.description: A memory limit for its machines, a string. The plugin's memory when absent.

ociRuntime.description: The OCI runtime Docker starts its machines under, a string. runsc is gVisor. Docker's own default when absent.

runtime.description: What makes its machines: docker, a container on the server's Docker; libvirt, a VM on the server's libvirt, as the libvirt option says; proxmox, a VM on the proxmox option's node, reached through the server when one is named. docker when absent.

server.description: The box its machines are made on, by its name in ssh.machines. The box is checked before a machine is made there. This host when absent.

code.description: How a machine on a server is given the session's code: bundle sends the tree's commit from this host; clone has the machine fetch the session's branch from origin over https, so only a public repository. bundle when absent.

workdir.description: Where commands start, a string. folder, or the image's own, when absent.

mounts.description: Mounts added after the plugin's own, a list of strings.

agents.description: The agents its machines are prepared for, a list of provider ids. A session of another agent is refused.

folder.description: A host folder mounted at the same path inside the machine, a string.

host.description: The command that starts the nested host inside one of its machines, a list of strings. ["ahpd"] when absent.

disposable.description: true: no machine until a session starts, and one is made for that session. false when absent.

disposableDelay.description: Milliseconds after the last session leaves a disposable machine before it is removed, a whole number above 0. 300000 when absent.

disposableAlone.description: true: a disposable machine is kept out of the picker, so only the session it was made for runs in it. false when absent.

sessionFolder.description: true: the session's working folder is mounted read-write at the same path inside the machine. false when absent.

sessionRepository.description: true: the repository that folder sits inside is mounted too. Needs sessionFolder. false when absent.

sessionTree.description: shared mounts this host's tree; copy gives the machine a checkout of its own that reaches the host only by fetch. Needs sessionFolder. shared when absent.

parts.description: The parts every machine from this profile carries, by their ids in the versions file.

secretUnreadable.description: When a need value named from the vault cannot be read again after a restart: fail every command into the machine, or drop that variable and log it. fail when absent.

state.description: Where its agents keep their state: volume, a named volume per provider seeded from this host, or host, this host's own configuration mounted. volume when absent.

stateScope.description: Who shares a state volume: owner, one per owner of the machine, or shared, one for every owner of the profile. owner when absent.

gitGuard.description: How a git directory in a session's machine is guarded: fetch, the machine committing in a git directory of its own so the host fetches the work back, or open, the host's git directory writable in the machine. fetch when absent. bind is read as fetch.

nestedDelete.description: Deleting a session that ran in a machine from this profile and is not running: inside, start the machine's own host to dispose that session there too, or record, delete it here and leave the machine's copy. inside when absent.

profiles.description: The named sets a person picks from when making a machine.

bodyMounts.description: Whether a person making a machine may name mounts of their own.

imageMounts.description: Whether a part may be mounted from its own image. false mounts every part from a volume filled once from it.

images.description: The images a machine may be made from, as containers-policy.json image scopes: docker.io/library/node:22 one image, docker.io/library/node a repository, ghcr.io/acme a namespace, ghcr.io a registry, *.example.com its subdomains.

source.description: The module specifier, or a path to a directory or a file.

name.description: What a listing prints, or the module in an entry written before source.

options.description: Passed to the plugin's apply as its second argument.

enabled.description: false drops the plugin before it is resolved. Absent means on.

grants.description: What the plugin may do when it connects as a client of its own.

plugins.description: The plugins the host inside the machine runs, as a module specifier or an object naming one. At least one, or the host inside has no backend.

devcontainer.description: The Dev Container CLI, as a launcher and as a machine maker, and the folders it may make one from; false switches every dev container route off.
